Operatives of the Delta State Police Command have shot dead two suspected kidnappers during a gun battle in a forest in Edo-Ogwashi, following the abduction of a 30-year-old man. The suspects were killed on November 15, three days after the victim, whose name was withheld, was abducted in the community. The police operatives, attached to the Special Anti-Kidnapping Unit, Sector III, Ubulu-Uku, reportedly acted on intelligence and collaborated with a human rights activist and members of the Ubulu-Uku community vigilante to track the suspects to their hideout in the Edo-Ogwashi forest. The suspects reportedly opened fire on the security team upon sighting them, leading to a gun battle in which two of them sustained gunshot injuries, while others escaped. The state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, confirmed the incident on Monday, saying, “One locally fabricated single-barrel gun, three live cartridges and part of the ransom paid were recovered.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. A search of the suspect reportedly led to the recovery of an English pistol, a locally made cut-to-size gun and three live cartridges. Edafe said the suspect was in police custody, while investigations were ongoing. Meanwhile, the state Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, commended members of the public “for volunteering credible information” and acknowledged the collaboration of community vigilante groups, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in tackling crime. He urged residents to “sustain this partnership with the Police in the collective interest of peace and security across the State.” Dele Ogunyemi Dele Ogunyemi is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over 25 years of experience in media practice.
